topology_reasoning.what: Two identical waveguides, mirror-symmetric about the horizontal midline. Each enters straight, S-bends toward the center, runs briefly parallel at a small gap (the coupling region), then S-bends back out. Classic directional coupler.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: Light in one guide evanescently couples to the other where the guides run close; the power transfer ratio is set by the gap, the parallel coupling length, and the effective interaction added by the slowly-converging S-bends. The S-bends also set input/output port separation so the ports are optically isolated.
function_knobs: wg_width_um: guide width, sets mode confinement (measured ~0.665 um; 0.666 on 2-dbu grid)
gap_um: edge-to-edge gap in the coupling region, dominant knob for coupling strength (final 0.30 um)
coupling_len_um: length of the close-parallel section (final 0.8 um)
sbend_len_um: S-bend length, controls adiabaticity + residual bend coupling (final 8.6 um)
io_sep_um: input/output center-to-center port separation (2.342 um)

measurements_px.calibration: 88.0 px/um in x, 149.0 px/um in y (anisotropic source raster), bbox 1584x447 px = 18x3 um
measurements_px.profile_fit: centerline least-squares fit strongly prefers sine S-bend y ~ t - sin(2 pi t)/(2 pi) over raised-cosine; symmetric-constrained fit: straight_in=0.006, sbend_len=8.596, coupling_len=0.796 (sse 0.035 vs 0.048)

iterations.change_made: initial build: raised-cosine S-bend, wg_width 0.666 (grid-snapped from 0.665), gap 0.29, coupling 1.4, sbend 7.3, straight_in 1.0; diff showed red outside / blue inside of every bend = my S-bend lags the target
switched to sine S-bend profile and adopted least-squares fit params: straight_in 0.0, sbend_len 8.6, coupling_len 0.8
gap 0.29 -> 0.30 (diff showed ~1px excess toward center at the waist)
tried wg_width 0.670 — worse; REVERTED to 0.666. Final = iter-3 config

knob_verification.width_um_note: 1.332 = 2 x wg_width_um (0.666): extending the coupling section lengthens BOTH guides, so area grows at twice the single-guide rate; single-guide width would mis-state the expected area growth by 2x
